newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bougainville's outcast miner still turns a profit.
newsitem.headline: Bougainville's outcast miner still turns a profit.

text.p: The operator of crisis-torn Papua New Guinea's defunct Bougainville copper mine may have no longer be producing metal, but it is still mining profits.

Bougainville Copper Ltd, which has not mined a pound of copper since it was chased off Bougainville island in 1989 by a secessionist uprising, turned a 5.7 million kina (US$4.1 million) net profit for calendar 1996, its annual report shows.
Virtually all of the company's revenue since abandoning its huge Panguna copper-gold deposit on the island's mountainous south has come from interest earned on short-term deposits.

That stockpile of cash has helped the company turn a profit for the last three years, but Bougainville Copper, controlled by global miner RTZ-CRA, warns in its latest annual report that further asset write-downs may one day hit the bottom line.
Mine equipment at the Panguna site has been left to rust since May 1989, when the mine was closed after it became the target of guerrilla attacks.
"With the passage of time and the continued actions of the militants, further deterioration of assets has undoubtedly taken place," Bougainville Copper chairman David Karpin said in the report.

The report was issued to the Australian Stock Exchange on Tuesday, as Papua New Guinea plunged into its deepest political political crisis yet over Bougainville with the army resisting the government's use of foreign mercenaries in the conflict.
Karpin was not immediately available for comment on Wednesday, but he sounded a pessimistic note in the report.
"During 1996...there has been no apparent progress made to find a peaceful solution," he said.

The Panguna mine produced 552,000 dry tonnes of copper concentrate in 1988, its last full year of operation, and is still sitting above 500 million tonnes of recoverable ore at an average grade of 0.42 percent copper.
